records.name: Green Light Productions
records.summary: A theatre company that makes plays and performance pieces written and directed by women. The public way in is seeing a show or sending in a script.
records.notes: Not a group under the arts rule: a production company with no class, membership, volunteer or community program on its site. Newest dated item is 2020 (Vital Records at the Bridge PHL Theatre Festival, month not shown), so last_sign_of_life is left out. A 'GLO IV' ticket date (October 16th) has no year and is not used. The founder's personal email on the site is deliberately not copied. Only the homepage was read; no further pages were checked.

records.name: Guacamaya International Aid
records.summary: A charity that helps vulnerable people in Venezuela with food, education and a monthly medical clinic in Aragua state.
records.notes: All programs are in Venezuela. Philadelphia appears only as the mailing address (P.O. Box 31421, 19147). IRS address is 704 N 18th Street Apt B. No dated items on the page.

records.name: Hispanic Bar Association of Pennsylvania
records.summary: A professional group for Hispanic and Latino lawyers, law students and others who care about the community. Its Legal Education Fund gives scholarships.
records.what_you_do: Come to the yearly scholarship banquet, join as a member, or send a message through the website's contact page.

schedule.text: Yearly scholarship banquet. The 36th was listed for October 1, 2026.

cost.text: Membership dues apply; the amount is not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Check the Membership Dues page on hbapa.net, then use the contact page to ask how someone who is not a lawyer can join.
first_step.basis: Open to attorneys, law students and other interested people, but membership is paid through dues and the page does not describe what a first event is like.

records.notes: IRS data name is truncated ('Legal Educational Fun'). The fund is also called HBALEF on the site. The banquet is marked Save the Date for October 1, 2026, which has passed as of 2026-10-08; the next date is not shown. Left out: the mailing address (P.O. Box 58399, a box is not a meeting place) and a regional liaison's personal email. The /lef-info/ path returned 404, so the home page was read instead.

records.name: Independence Squares
records.summary: A square dance club for LGBTQ+ dancers in Philadelphia. Members dance modern Western square dance, and partners change about every 15 minutes, so you can come without a partner.
records.what_you_do: Take a beginner class in the fall, come to a summer open house, or join the Tuesday evening classes and dances. Saturday dances run at several levels, so check the dance schedule before you go.

schedule.text: Tuesday classes and workshops, 7 to 9:30 pm, for beginners and experienced dancers. Beginner classes start each September and run until spring. Saturday dances fall on certain dates through the year; see the dance schedule.

locations.label: Lutheran Church of the Holy Communion (most dances)

cost.text: About $10 for one dance session, $15 for both sessions of a two-session event, and usually $5 for open houses. Reduced admission is available by application.

first_step.how: Come to a Tuesday class at 2111 Sansom St at 7 pm, or to a summer open house. No partner is needed; join the nearest square when the music starts.
first_step.basis: The page says newcomers are welcome, runs beginner classes each fall and open houses in summer for beginners, and says no partner is needed.

records.notes: The dance schedule lists dances on Saturday October 17, 2026 and December 5, 2026, plus 2027 dates, so the club is planning ahead. The newest dated item on the home page is a fly-in registration post dated 2026/03/13 (date taken from the post link). The classes page was not read, so the beginner class price is not shown. The email is the club's own published address.

records.name: HFTP Greater Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a national group for people who work in hospitality finance and technology. It holds chapter meetings and education events, and it supports local hospitality students with a scholarship.
records.what_you_do: Go to a chapter meeting or education event to meet peers. The site promotes membership for career and certification resources but does not list dues.

cost.text: Dues are not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Use the contact link on hftpphila.org to ask about the next chapter meeting and how to join. The email address is hidden on the page, so the contact form is the way in.
first_step.basis: Membership is promoted, but the page does not show dues, a join step or a public event schedule, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Legal name is International Association of Hospitality Accountants. The one event on the site, a Save the Date for a Wednesday October 21st at Aronimink, has no year shown, so it is not used as dated evidence. The footer copyright reads 2020 and is not used either. Status is probably_active only because the site loads with no dated items. Mailing address is PO Box 22386 (19110); left out of locations because it is not a meeting place.

records.name: Deaf Apostolate, Archdiocese of Philadelphia
records.summary: The Catholic Church's ministry for Deaf and hard of hearing Catholics in the Philadelphia area. It offers Mass and sacraments in American Sign Language, pastoral care and religious education.
records.what_you_do: Call ahead to ask for current Mass times and churches in American Sign Language. The sources found do not show current times.

first_step.how: Call the Deaf Apostolate at 215-587-3913, or use the video phone at 267-507-1215, and ask for the current ASL Mass times and locations.
first_step.basis: The ministry serves Deaf and hard of hearing Catholics and gives a phone and video phone line to ask how to join. The sources found do not say whether newcomers are specifically welcomed.

records.notes: The batch website deafcatholicphilly.org refused connections on two tries (with and without www). A search found the Archdiocese of Philadelphia's Deaf Apostolate. The director named there matches the batch contact (Sister Kathleen Schipani), so this record is matched on that name only. Not confirmed as the same legal entity as the IRS record. Facts come from the search excerpt; the page itself was not fetched. The Mass details come from a 2020 report. A named staff member's email is left out; call instead. Status unknown until someone confirms the ministry is current.

records.name: Investing in Ourselves
records.summary: A group that teaches money and investing skills to community members. Its weekly investment club meets on Zoom, and past meetings are recorded for people who cannot attend live.
records.what_you_do: Join the Thursday investment club on Zoom, watch past meetings in the Meeting Library, or book a one on one appointment through the site.

schedule.text: Investment club meets every Thursday at 6 pm Eastern time on Zoom.

first_step.how: Join the Thursday 6 pm investment club on Zoom. The join link is on investinginourselves.org, and the Meeting Library has recordings if you cannot come live.
first_step.basis: A public Zoom meeting with a join link on the site, plus recordings for people who cannot attend. The page does not say whether beginners are specifically welcome.

records.notes: The site header also uses the name Bridges to Wealth. Status is probably_active because the site is current but has no dated items. The only dated mention is a 2019 pitch competition in a photo caption; the footer copyright is not used. The page does not state a Philadelphia service area. The IRS record has a Philadelphia address (2114 Cherry Street), and the site names United Way of Greater Philadelphia and Southern New Jersey as a partner. The entrepreneur program runs once a year and has a waitlist. No street address written as a location because the page shows none.
